label: Tarajal Breakwater
sub: Main crossing point where thousands swam or waded into Ceuta on Jul 30-31, 2026, past the border fence and Moroccan checkpoints.

label: Benzú Breakwater
sub: Secondary swimming crossing point on Ceuta's northern coastline used heavily during the July 30-31 surge.

label: Fnideq Staging Ground
sub: Moroccan border town where migrants gathered before crossing; Moroccan forces later closed access routes and dispersed crowds here.

label: Bni Nsar Clashes
sub: Moroccan town bordering Melilla where migrants clashed with police, throwing rocks and setting police vehicles ablaze on Jul 30.

label: Beni Ansar Crossing (Melilla)
sub: Melilla's only operating land border post, temporarily closed Jul 30 amid crowding and clashes, disrupting summer travel.

label: CETI Reception Centre
sub: Temporary Immigrant Reception Centre, capacity 512, held 700+ with hundreds more camped outside without food or water for days.

label: Unaccompanied Minors Shelter
sub: Facility for unaccompanied migrant minors, reported by Mayor Vivas as running at 2,400% of ordinary capacity; only 29 spots available for 862 minors by Aug 3.

label: Algeciras Transfer Hub
sub: Mainland Spain reception point for migrants ferried out of Ceuta; first group of 39 Sudanese nationals arrived here Jul 29.

label: Tarajal Drowning Site
sub: Site of the majority of the 88+ drowning deaths recorded within a 48-hour window during the crossing.

label: Fnideq Fatalities
sub: 11 of the 111 confirmed crisis deaths occurred on the Moroccan side, in and around Fnideq.

label: Ceuta University Hospital
sub: Treated crush and drowning injuries from the crossing; separately reported at least 5 migrant girls with injury indicators consistent with sexual assault.

label: Strait of Gibraltar Patrol Zone
sub: Frontex offered additional surveillance, registration and returns support across this maritime approach following the Aug 4 EU interior ministers meeting.

label: Ceuta Port — Italy/Portugal Checks
sub: Italian and Portuguese police deployed directly at Ceuta's ferry port from Aug 4 to inspect non-EU travellers before departure.

label: Madrid — Moncloa Palace
sub: Seat of Spain's government; site of crisis coordination, the €25M minors fund announcement, and Italy's ambassador being summoned.

label: Rabat — Moroccan Government
sub: Morocco's government expressed regret, denied deliberately facilitating the crossing, and blamed smuggling networks and viral misinformation.

label: Rome — Schengen Suspension Announced
sub: Meloni, Salvini and Tajani announced Italy's suspension of Schengen free movement with Spain, effective Aug 1.

label: Brussels — EU Emergency Talks
sub: European Commission and interior ministers held the Aug 4 crisis videoconference; von der Leyen called the images from Ceuta 'unacceptable.'

label: Paris — Reinforced Border Checks
sub: France reimposed border checks Jul 31 while Macron voiced solidarity with Sánchez and praised Moroccan cooperation on returns.

label: Vienna — Border Closure Threat
sub: Chancellor Christian Stocker warned Austria could 'temporarily close' its borders; Family Minister Claudia Bauer accused Spain of 'handing out entry tickets.'

label: Algiers — Sánchez Visit (Jul 20)
sub: Sánchez's reconciliation visit to Algeria on Jul 20, widely cited as the trigger Morocco was retaliating against ten days later.

label: Castillejos Dispersal Site
sub: Mountainous area southwest of Ceuta, outside Fnideq, where Moroccan forces backed by navy boats and drones broke up a 294-person regrouping attempt on Aug 16.

label: El Trampolín Beach Camp
sub: Informal camp where thousands of migrants slept rough after the July 30-31 crossing. Police cleared it Aug 20, but migrants returned within hours after both the Aug 20 and Aug 21 eviction attempts and fully rebuilt the camp by Aug 22. On Aug 26-27, residents blocked a Red Cross food truck here for over two hours, then broke through a police cordon at adjacent Benítez beach, stormed the camp and set fire to migrants' straw shelters.

label: Loma Margarita Shelter
sub: One of two new temporary reception centres (1,800 combined initial capacity) opened Aug 20 to house migrants relocated from the El Trampolín beach camp.

label: El Embolsamiento Shelter
sub: Second of two new temporary reception centres opened Aug 20 alongside Loma Margarita to receive migrants cleared from the beach camp.

label: Benzú — Soldiers Ambushed
sub: A Spanish military vehicle carrying four soldiers was ambushed by roughly 70 migrants throwing stones early on Aug 27; one soldier suffered minor injuries. Police detained 12 Moroccan nationals — the first reported assault on Spanish security forces since the July 30-31 crossing.
